A FUNK PERSPECTIVE ON BILLIARDS, PROJECTIVE
GEOMETRY AND MAHLER VOLUME
DMITRY FAIFMAN
Abstract. We explore connections furnished by the Funk metric, a relative
of the Hilbert metric, between projective geometry, billiards, convex geome-
try and aﬃne inequalities. We ﬁrst show that many metric invariants of the
Funk metric are invariant under projective maps, as well as under projective
duality. These include the Holmes-Thompson volume and surface area of con-
vex subsets, and the length spectrum of their boundary, extending results of
Holmes-Thompson and ´Alvarez Paiva on Sch¨aﬀer’s dual girth

blocks.title: Funk and Hilbert metrics
blocks.content:
The Hilbert metric in the interior of a convex set $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ is given by $$d^H_K(x,y)=\frac12 \log \frac{|ay||xb|}{|ax||yb|},$$ where $a,x,y,b$ appear in that order on the line through $x,y$ with $a,b\in\partial K$. It is evidently invariant under invertible projective maps. Hilbert discovered this metric while attempting to generalize the Beltrami-Klein model of hyperbolic geometry. It is moreover a *projective* metric, meaning that straight segments are geodesic. Hilbert's fourth problem [@hilbert_problems] asks for a construction of all projective metrics.

blocks.title: Summary of results
blocks.content:
If $K\subset\mathbb{R}\mathbb{P}^n$ is a convex body with interior, we may fix a hyperplane at infinity $\eta$ that is disjoint from $K$, and consider the corresponding $\eta$-Funk metric on $K$, denoted $\mathop{\mathrm{Funk}}_K^\eta$. Changing $\eta$ results in a change to the Funk metric, but of a very particular type: the Finsler norm is changed by an exact 1-form. This is the core reason behind the projective invariance of many metric invariants associated to the Funk metric, as follows.

blocks.title: Convexity
blocks.content:
A convex body $K\subset V=\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact convex set, which we will henceforth assume to have non-empty interior. We write $|K|$ for the Euclidean volume of $K$, and $\mathcal H^{n-1}$ for the Hausdorff measure on $\partial K$.

The Euclidean unit ball is $B^n$, and $\omega_n:=|B^n|=\frac{\pi^{\frac n 2}}{\Gamma(\frac n 2 +1)}$. The support function of $K\subset V$ is $h_K(\xi)=\sup_{x\in K}\langle x,\xi\rangle:V^*\to \mathbb{R}$, which is a convex function. We say that $K$ is smooth and strictly convex if $\partial K$ is $C^2$-smooth of strictly positive gaussian curvature.

blocks.title: Finsler geometry
blocks.content:
A *non-reversible Finsler manifold* $(M,\phi)$ is a smooth manifold equipped with a function $\phi :TM\setminus \underline 0\to [0,\infty)$, which restricts to a non-symmetric norm on each tangent space. The assumed smoothness of $\phi$ depends on the problem at hand.

The tangent unit ball at $x$ is $B_xM=\{v\in T_xM: \phi(x,v)\leq 1\}$, and the cotangent ball is $B_x^*M=(B_xM)^o\subset T_x^*M$. The co-ball bundle is $B^*M=\cup_{x\in M}B_x^*M$.

The Gutkin-Tabachnikov duality of Minkowski billiards has a continuous counterpart, namely Schäffer's dual girth conjecture [@schaeffer], which is a theorem of Álvarez Paiva [@alvarez-paiva]. blocks.title: Mahler volumes of every Funk scale
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:every_scale label="sec:every_scale"} Define the *Funk-Mahler volume of radius $0<r<\infty$ (around $q\in \mathop{\mathrm{int}}(K)$)* by $$M_r(K,q)=\omega_n r^{-n}\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}_K^F(B_r^F(q, K)), \quad  M_r(K)=\inf_{q\in \mathop{\mathrm{int}}(K)}M_r(K,q).$$

In Euclidean terms, we have $$M_r(K,q)=r^{-n}\int_{z\in q+(1-e^{-r})(K-q)}|K^z|dz,$$ where $K^z$ denotes the dual body with respect to $z$. Evidently, $M_r(K,q)$ is invariant under the full linear group with $q$ at the origin.
